{{Short description|German plant biologist}}
{{orphan|date=September 2026}}

'''Stefan Andreas Rensing''' (born June 1967) is a German plant [[biologist]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Zimmer |first=Carl |date=2019-11-14 |title=How Did Plants Conquer Land? These Humble Algae Hold Clues |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/14/science/plant-genes-evolution.html |access-date=2026-07-31 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> [[bioinformatician]], and [[Academic administration|university administrator]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maldacker |first=Anika |date=2021-02-08 |title=Zellbiologe Stefan Rensing wird Prorektor der Uni Freiburg |url=https://www.badische-zeitung.de/zellbiologe-stefan-rensing-wird-prorektor-der-uni-freiburg |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=Badische Zeitung |language=de}}</ref> He is professor of Data Integration and Systems Modelling of Eukaryotic Model Organisms at the [[University of Freiburg]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Stefan Rensing becomes Vice President for Research and Innovation - BIOSS |url=https://www.bioss.uni-freiburg.de/stefan-rensing-becomes-vice-president-for-research-and-innovation/ |access-date=2026-07-30 |language=en-GB}}</ref> His research focuses on [[plant evolution]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Claussen |first=Arne |date=2022-06-20 |title=Trends in Plant Science cover story: evolutionary biology |url=https://www.hhu.de/en/news-article/the-greening-ashore |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=www.hhu.de |language=de}}</ref> [[comparative genomics]],<ref name=":22">{{Cite news |last=Bi |first=Guiqi |title=Researchers present near-complete genome version of spreading earth moss |url=https://phys.org/news/2024-02-genome-version-earth-moss.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240209162034/https://phys.org/news/2024-02-genome-version-earth-moss.html |archive-date=2024-02-09 |access-date=2026-07-30 |language=en}}</ref> [[bioinformatics]], and [[systems biology]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mueller |first=Kim-Kristine |last2=Pfeifer |first2=Lukas |last3=Wegner |first3=Linus |last4=Ehlers |first4=Katrin |last5=Classen |first5=Birgit |date=2025 |title=New insights into bryophyte arabinogalactan-proteins from a hornwort and a moss model organism |url=https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12209756/ |journal=The Plant Journal: For Cell and Molecular Biology |volume=123 |issue=1 |article-number=e70312 |doi=10.1111/tpj.70312 |issn=1365-313X |pmc=12209756 |pmid=40589202}}</ref>

He is a member of [[German Society for Plant Sciences|German Botanical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pucker |first=Boas |title=Executive and Extended Committee (2025 - 2026) |url=https://www.deutsche-botanische-gesellschaft.de/en/about-us/board-of-the-dbg/board-2025-2026 |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=www.deutsche-botanische-gesellschaft.de}}</ref> the European Plant Science Organisation (EPSO), the [[International Association of Bryologists]] (IAB), the International Society of Endocytobiology (ISE), and the German Life Sciences Association (VBIO).<ref>{{Cite web |title=plantco.de - the Rensing lab pages |url=https://plantco.de/people/Stefan.php |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=plantco.de}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Rensing studied biology at the [[University of Freiburg]], receiving a Diplom degree in 1993. He completed his doctoral degree (''Dr. rer. nat.'') in [[cell biology]] in 1995 under the supervision of Peter Sitte and Uwe-G. Maier. In 2007, he obtained his habilitation in [[bioinformatics]] and [[systems biology]] from the [[University of Freiburg]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. rer. nat. Stefan A. Rensing |url=https://www.bioss.uni-freiburg.de/wp-content/uploads/CV_Rensing_2023.pdf |website=BIOSS}}</ref>

He served as a senior scientist and laboratory head at BASF Plant Science and the University of Freiburg, where he worked on [[functional genomics]] using the moss ''[[Physcomitrella patens|Physcomitrium patens]]''.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /> Between 2007 and 2008, Rensing directed the Core Facility for Data Management within the Freiburg Initiative for Systems Biology (FRISYS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Freiburg Initiative for Systems Biology Performs Transcriptomics with Genedata Expressionist |url=https://www.genedata.com/company/news/details/press-release/frisys-performs-transcriptomics |access-date=2026-07-31 |website=www.genedata.com}}</ref>

In 2012, Rensing was appointed Professor of Plant Cell Biology at the [[Marburg University|University of Marburg]]. He was promoted to a W3 professorship in 2019 and served as Vice Dean and  then Dean of the Department of Biology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Section Plant Physiology and Molecular Biology in the DBG |url=https://www.pflanzen-molekularbiologie.de/en/kategorie/sppmb |access-date=2026-07-31 |website=www.pflanzen-molekularbiologie.de |language=en-EN}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

== Research and scholarly work ==
Rensing's research focuses on [[plant evolution]],<ref name=":0" /> [[comparative genomics]],<ref name=":22"/> [[bioinformatics]], [[systems biology]], and [[Plant biology|molecular plant biology]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Steiner |first=Von Thomas |date=2023-10-25 |title=Es ist erstaunlich, was an der Universität Freiburg alles geforscht wird |url=https://www.badische-zeitung.de/es-ist-erstaunlich-was-an-der-universitaet-freiburg-alles-geforscht-wird |access-date=2026-07-31 |website=Badische Zeitung |language=de}}</ref> Much of his work has centered on [[bryophytes]], particularly the [[Physcomitrella patens|moss ''Physcomitrium patens'']] (formerly ''Physcomitrella patens''), which he has helped establish as a model organism for studying plant evolution, development, and the transition of plants from aquatic to terrestrial environments.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rensing |first=Stefan A. |last2=Goffinet |first2=Bernard |last3=Meyberg |first3=Rabea |last4=Wu |first4=Shu-Zon |last5=Bezanilla |first5=Magdalena |date=2020 |title=The Moss Physcomitrium (Physcomitrella) patens: A Model Organism for Non-Seed Plants |url=https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7203925/ |journal=The Plant Cell |volume=32 |issue=5 |pages=1361–1376 |doi=10.1105/tpc.19.00828 |issn=1532-298X |pmc=7203925 |pmid=32152187}}</ref> His research integrates [[genome sequencing]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Price |first=D. C. |title=Origin of photosynthesis revealed by a &apos;living fossil&apos; |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/02/120217101339.htm |access-date=2026-07-31 |website=ScienceDaily |language=en}}</ref> [[Transcriptomics technologies|transcriptomics]], [[phylogenomics]], and computational biology to investigate the origins and diversification of land plants.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zeitung |first=Badische |date=2025-01-22 |title=Freiburger Forscher sollen Landwirtschaft widerstandsfähig machen und bekommen Geld vom Land |url=https://www.badische-zeitung.de/freiburger-forscher-sollen-landwirtschaft-widerstandsfaehig-machen-und-bekommen-geld-vom-land |access-date=2026-07-31 |website=Badische Zeitung |language=de}}</ref>

Rensing has contributed to international genome sequencing and comparative genomics projects involving [[plants]], [[algae]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ying |first=Irene |title=International collaboration finds land plant genes in ancient aquatic alga |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/762237 |access-date=2026-07-31 |website=Eureka}}</ref> [[fungi]], and other [[Eukaryote|eukaryotic organisms]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sun |first=Guiling |last2=Bai |first2=Shenglong |last3=Guan |first3=Yanlong |last4=Wang |first4=Shuanghua |last5=Wang |first5=Qia |last6=Liu |first6=Yang |last7=Liu |first7=Huan |last8=Goffinet |first8=Bernard |last9=Zhou |first9=Yun |last10=Paoletti |first10=Mathieu |last11=Hu |first11=Xiangyang |last12=Haas |first12=Fabian B. |last13=Fernandez-Pozo |first13=Noe |last14=Czyrt |first14=Alia |last15=Sun |first15=Hang |date=2020 |title=Are fungi-derived genomic regions related to antagonism towards fungi in mosses? |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/nph.16776 |journal=New Phytologist |language=en |volume=228 |issue=4 |pages=1169–1175 |doi=10.1111/nph.16776 |issn=1469-8137}}</ref> He has participated in genome consortia for species including ''[[Physcomitrella patens|Physcomitrium patens]]'',<ref name=":22"/> ''[[Ceratodon purpureus]]'', ''[[Funaria hygrometrica]]'',<ref>{{Citation |last=Kirbis |first=Alexander |title=Genome dynamics in mosses: Extensive synteny coexists with a highly dynamic gene space |date=2022-05-18 |url=https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.05.17.492078v1 |access-date=2026-07-31 |publisher=bioRxiv |language=en |doi=10.1101/2022.05.17.492078 |last2=Rahmatpour |first2=Nasim |last3=Dong |first3=Shanshan |last4=Yu |first4=Jin |last5=Gessel |first5=Nico van |last6=Waller |first6=Manuel |last7=Reski |first7=Ralf |last8=Lang |first8=Daniel |last9=Rensing |first9=Stefan A.|pmc=11871058 }}</ref> ''Takakia lepidozioides'', ''Selaginella moellendorffii'', ''Chara braunii'', ''Azolla filiculoides'' and ''Volvox carteri.''
